sec:archimedean-lifting-intro:
The preceding sections established lifting, descent, and mass over a generic ring R. This section restricts to R = \mathbb{R}. The brane tower geometrically realizes a sequence of smooth jet bundles J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, reducing the categorical mass identity to a nonabelian multiplicative integral.

Smooth jet prolongation frames J^1\mathcal{S}_n as the geometric carrier of A_n. The Yekutieli extension fixes the band \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}. The smooth proof of the \mathrm{QU} \Rightarrow \mathrm{QOU} specialisation instantiates the main theorem for \mathrm{SU}_q(2) frame bundles.

Two structural lemmas support the mass programme. The smooth Euler characteristic stability verifies the \chi(A_n) proposition. The defining boundary structure isolates the codimension and chirality data of the brane boundary.
cor:jet-prolongation-C:
Corollary Archimedean realisation of jet prolongation. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be an archimedean quantum observable universe (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) equipped with an instanton connection A on the principal bundle P and a metric g on \mathcal{S}. One denotes the total space of \mathcal{S} by \widetilde{M} = \mathcal{S}. Let P' be the frame bundle and \mathcal{S}' the bundle of orthonormal frames of the first jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}. The data (A, g) uniquely determines a connection A' on P' such that (\mathbf{C}, \tilde\varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}') structurally forms an archimedean quantum observable universe.

Dimension preservation is one of the defining conditions of a jet prolongation, not a consequence of the others: prolonged and base are independent data, so nothing forces their CR dimensions to agree except the condition itself. The statement returns that condition under a readable name and derives nothing. Read the statement as fixing what a prolongation is, not as a corollary of the construction.
prf:jet-prolongation-C: Proof Proof of Archimedean realisation of jet prolongation. Apply jet prolongation to the categorical data (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) underlying the archimedean quantum observable universe (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) with aether parameter q. Here, \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_{q}(2)), A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)), and \tau is the forgetful functor. The fibre functor \tau translates the categorical jet object J^1(A) into the geometric first jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}, the inherited Frobenius–Hopf structure into the connection A', and the non-degeneracy and vanishing conditions into the analytic criteria of a \mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe.
rem:yekutieli-archimedean-band: Remark Archimedean band of the gerbe extension. In the archimedean realisation (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe), the banding sheaf specializes to \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}, the sheaf of invertible holomorphic functions on M.
prf:qu-to-qou:
Proof Proof of QU with observability and categorical lifting is a QOU. Yekutieli lifting establishes that the constructed brane tower satisfies the Quantum lifting condition. One proves each structural property in turn.

Item (1): Descent terminates. The centre Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)) is a finitely generated commutative R-algebra (since R is Noetherian and \tau is faithful), hence has finite Krull dimension d_0. Observability forces the G_q-action on A to be faithful: any G_q-invariant element of \mathrm{Ad}(A) would give a non-zero element of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)). Each descent step strictly reduces the Krull dimension of the centre, so after at most d_0 steps the base becomes a discrete (Artinian) scheme.

Item (2): \kappa_0 equals the Euler class. On a manifold the sheaf \underline{\mathbb{R}} of smooth real functions is fine, so H^k(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathbb{R}}) = 0 for k \geq 1. Every \underline{\mathbb{R}}-torsor is therefore trivial. The connecting map of 1 \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{\mathbb{R}} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} \to 1 is an isomorphism \delta \colon H^1(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)}) \to H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}), and it sends the class of \xi to c_1(\xi). So \xi lifts along \underline{\mathbb{R}} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} exactly when c_1(\xi) = 0, and the obstruction is \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi). For an oriented circle bundle, c_1 = e. When \xi is the unit tangent bundle, e(\xi)[\mathcal{S}] = \chi(\mathcal{S}) by Poincaré--Hopf. This is the torsor instance of the lifting theorem for central extensions of gerbes (Yekutieli 2010, Example "torsors" and Theorem 4.17). On Bring's surface, \kappa_0 = -6.

Item (3): Kummer persistence. Taking n-th powers is a surjection of sheaves \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)}, since n-th roots exist locally. Its kernel is the constant sheaf \mu_n. The long exact sequence contains

  H^1(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)})
   \xrightarrow{\;n\;}
  H^1(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)})
   \longrightarrow
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n)
   \longrightarrow
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)}).

By item (2), H^1(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)}) \cong H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}. Similarly H^2(\mathcal{S}, \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)}) \cong H^3(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) = 0 for a surface. So H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n. The obstruction to an n-th root of \xi is the image of c_1(\xi) = \chi(\mathcal{S}), namely \chi(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n. It vanishes exactly when n \mid \chi(\mathcal{S}). For \chi(\mathcal{S}) \neq 0 that happens for finitely many n. On Bring's surface those are n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}; the case n = 2 is a spin structure.

Comparison with the jet-prolongation tower. On a closed surface such as Bring's surface, no complementary-subgroup decomposition separates \kappa_0 from additive jet corrections inside H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}):

  • The additive corrections lie in the image of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}) = 0.
  • The group H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} has no non-trivial direct-sum complement.
  • The archimedean band \mathcal{O}^{\times} satisfies H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) = 0.

Cohomological persistence of \kappa_0 therefore holds in the Kummer tower of item (3) rather than at every level of the jet tower. In the jet tower, the holomorphic extension classes of the tangent bundle are non-zero at every level except n = 3; see the remark on jet-tower splitting.

Item (4): Riemann--Hurwitz. The branched covering \pi \colon S \to \mathbb{P}(V) of degree d has total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2d + \lvert\chi(A)\rvert by Riemann--Hurwitz: \chi(S) = d \cdot \chi(\mathbb{P}(V)) - R_{\mathrm{tot}} with \chi(\mathbb{P}(V)) = 2.

Item (5): Terminal fiber data. At a branch point p, the Krull dimension of the centre is 0, so the base is a point. The QOU data reduces to the fiber: the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A at parameter q(p), with the involution \sigma \colon \mathbb{P}(V) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Ad}(A) of fibre adjoint involution. \square

Item (6): Lifting criterion. This is proved for a central extension of presheaves of groups that is exact and central on every section group, and a cocycle with a local lift on overlaps. The obstruction is a 2-cocycle. Its class does not depend on the local lift, and it is compatible with refinement of the cover.
prf:euler-char-stability-C:
Proof Archimedean proof of Euler characteristic stability. Part (2). In the archimedean realisation the tower is a sequence of bundles over the fixed base M_0. By the explicit construction of the recursive brane tower, \mathcal{S}_{n+1} is the bundle of orthonormal frames of the first jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}_n (jet prolongation), projectivised; its typical fibre is \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2.

The Euler characteristic of a fibre bundle F \hookrightarrow E \to B whose fibre has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex and whose monodromy acts trivially on H^*(F; \mathbb{Q}) is multiplicative, \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(E) = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(F) \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(B) (the Leray–Serre spectral sequence collapses at E_2). The observability axiom \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 is what makes the monodromy of \pi_1(\mathcal{S}_n) on H^*(S^2; \mathbb{Z}) trivial: the adjoint bundle has no invariant sections to twist the fibre cohomology. Since \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(S^2) = 2,

  \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_{n+1}) = 2\,\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n),

so the Euler characteristic of the total space doubles at every level and is not the stable quantity.

What is stable is the base. Each level of the tower replaces a bundle over M_0 by a bundle over M_0 and never alters M_0; therefore \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) persists at every level. \square
prf:brane-boundary:
Proof Proof of Structure of the defining boundary. (1). The descent map \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} is a surjective *-homomorphism of fibre algebras (descent). Its kernel is zero generically because the ascent \ell_n embeds A as a direct summand of J^1(A), with r_n acting as the left-inverse. The kernel is non-trivial only where this splitting degenerates—a closed algebraic condition on the Frobenius pairing \varepsilon \circ m. Since A is a Frobenius--Hopf object in a rigid monoidal category, standard vector-bundle degeneracy bounds give this locus a real codimension of at least 2.

(2). At a blow-up centre p \in \partial \mathcal{S}_n, \ker(r_n|_p) is the fibre of \Omega^1(A) over p modulo the image of \eta\colon \mathbf{1} \to A. Because \Omega^1(A) \hookrightarrow A \otimes A and A has fibre \mathrm{SU}(2), this quotient is isomorphic to the projectivisation of the 2-dimensional representation: \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2. This yields the exceptional divisor resolving the singularity at p.

(3). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} (descent involution) on J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1} restricts to the boundary locus \partial \mathcal{S}_n. Because \partial \mathcal{S}_n is defined by \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_p) \neq 0 and \hat{\tau}_n projects onto the image of \ell_n, the restriction \hat{\tau}_n|_{\partial \mathcal{S}_n} acts as an involution. Its fixed points are the sections entirely within the descended subalgebra—matching the monodromy fixed-point condition of the quantum characteristic classes.

(4). At n = 1, the base is M and \mathcal{S}_1 fibres over M with fibre \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong S^2. The boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_1 marks the locus where jet restriction degenerates. By (2), each fibre of \partial \mathcal{S}_1 is \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), separating base (spacetime) and fibre (chiral) coordinates. The Reeb vector field \xi is vertical, so the reversal \xi \mapsto -\xi exchanges the two sides of \partial \mathcal{S}_1. The positive Reeb eigenspace carries left-handed fermions, and the negative carries right-handed.
prose:outro-lifting-and-descent:
Chapter close — Lifting and Descent.

This concludes categorical lifting and descent. The framework has assembled the brane tower, while the descent involution recovers the physical algebra in the classical limit. The cosimplicial crossed groupoid elevates this arithmetic to a higher-categorical structure.

The subsequent chapter (Braids and Knots) consumes this brane tower. The algebraic level A_n carries the n-strand braid action, yielding the Hecke algebra at q \neq 1. The Yekutieli cocycle data introduced here controls the resulting knot category.
sec:path-integrals-intro:
This chapter initiates Part II by passing from Step 1 of the five-step arc (the rigid braided monoidal category (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) of Part I) to Step 2: the algebraic mechanics of the braid group B_n and its Iwahori–Hecke quotient H_n(q). In a quantum observable universe whose base and fibres have finite cohomological rank, continuum path integrals \int \mathcal{D}\phi are replaced by finite algebraic traces over braid operators acting on tensor powers A^{\otimes n} of the Frobenius–Hopf object. Because the trace is evaluated over a finite-dimensional algebra over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], ultraviolet divergences do not arise.

The braiding isomorphism c_{A,A} \colon A \otimes A \xrightarrow{\sim} A \otimes A induced by the universal R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation and generates a representation of Artin's braid group B_n. Factoring through the quadratic Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 yields the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q), equipped with the Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution and the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three-row Young weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically, forcing the three-strand antisymmetric channel to be evaluated via the Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Turaev modified trace.
sec:categorical-braiding:
Although Artin's braid group B_n is classically defined as the fundamental group of the configuration space of n distinct points in the plane, in a quantum observable universe braiding is an internal categorical datum that precedes any spatial manifold. Because the braiding isomorphism c_{X,Y} \colon X \otimes Y \xrightarrow{\sim} Y \otimes X is defined purely in terms of the monoidal structure of \mathbf{C}, it remains valid over arbitrary commutative base rings and non-Archimedean completions where topological knot complements are absent.

This section constructs the q-deformed braiding family on tensor powers A^{\otimes n} of the Frobenius–Hopf object, verifies the two Mac Lane hexagon coherence identities under the Reeb derivation, and demonstrates why three strands (B_3) form the minimal non-abelian arena in which the symmetric quotient S_3 separates into boson, fermion, and three-colour parities.
prop:braid-action-tensor:
Proposition Braid-group action on tensor powers. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe whose ambient category \mathbf{C} is braided monoidal with braiding c_{X,Y}\colon X\otimes Y \xrightarrow{ \sim } Y\otimes X. For each object V in \mathbf{C} and each n \geq 2, there is a group homomorphism

  \rho_n\colon B_n  \longrightarrow  \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes n})

given on the Artin generators by

\begin{equation}\label{eq:categorical-braid-rep}
  \rho_n(\sigma_i)
  = 
  \mathrm{id}^{\otimes(i-1)}
  \otimes c_{V,V}
  \otimes \mathrm{id}^{\otimes(n-i-1)},
  \qquad 1 \leq i \leq n-1.
\end{equation}

The braid relation \rho_n(\sigma_i)\rho_n(\sigma_{i+1})\rho_n(\sigma_i) = \rho_n(\sigma_{i+1})\rho_n(\sigma_i)\rho_n(\sigma_{i+1}) is mathematically equivalent to the Yang--Baxter equation for the braiding c_{V,V}.

The braid-group action itself is standard (e.g., Kassel, Theorem XIII.1.3).
prf:braid-action-tensor:
Proof Proof of Braid-group action on tensor powers. The hexagon axioms of a braided monoidal category guarantee that c_{V,V} satisfies the Yang--Baxter equation

  (c \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes c)
  \circ (c \otimes \mathrm{id})
  = 
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes c)
  \circ (c \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes c)

on V^{\otimes 3}. This is exactly the braid relation for adjacent generators, and the far-commutativity relation \sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i (\lvert i-j\rvert \geq 2) follows from the naturality of the braiding. Together these verify the Artin presentation of B_n.
rem:why-B3: Remark B_3 in the Descartes universe: rationale. The volume axiom forces the gauge group to be a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2) (SU(2) emergence), independently of the Descartes condition; \mathrm{SU}(2) has rank 1. Consequently, the fundamental representation V is 2-dimensional. On V^{\otimes 2}, the braiding provides a single operator c_{V,V}. The first non-trivial braid group action occurs on V^{\otimes 3}, where the two generators \sigma_1, \sigma_2 of B_3 act via the categorical braid representation.
rem:categorical-boson-fermion: Remark Categorical distinction between bosons and fermions. The Schur--Weyl decomposition V^{\otimes 3} \cong V_{\frac{3}{2}} \oplus V_{\frac{1}{2}}^{\oplus 2} separates the symmetric (spin-\frac{3}{2}) and mixed-symmetry (spin-\frac{1}{2}) sectors. The B_3-action preserves this decomposition. On the symmetric sector, the generators act as scalars, producing bosonic exchange. On the mixed-symmetry sector, they act non-trivially, producing fermionic exchange. This categorical distinction between bosons and fermions requires no topological input.
rem:symmetric-quotient-colour: Remark The symmetric quotient and colour sectors. The quotient B_3 \twoheadrightarrow S_3 obtained by imposing \sigma_i^2 = \mathrm{id} corresponds to passing from a braided monoidal category to a symmetric monoidal one, requiring c_{V,V}^2 = \mathrm{id}. In the Descartes universe, the three copies of S_3 inside S_5 = \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) are images of three such quotients. Each quotient corresponds to a colour sector \mathfrak{r}, \mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{b}. Lifting these three S_3 subgroups back to B_3 via the braiding of \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) recovers the non-trivial exchange phases that distinguish quarks from leptons.
prop:colour-singlet-flavour-generator:
Proposition On colour singlets the rescaled strand braid is the flavour Hecke generator. Let K be a field, q \in K with q \neq 0 and q^2 + 1 \neq 0, and let \check R be Jimbo's braiding of U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) on (K^3)^{\otimes n}. Let b be a flavour Hecke generator, (b - q)(b + q^{-1}) = 0, and let X = \check R_{\mathrm{colour}} \cdot b be the tensor braiding of a strand carrying colour and flavour.

  1. \check R satisfies the Hecke relation and the braid relation, and commutes with the coproducts of E_i, F_i and L_j.
  2. The colour singlets in (K^3)^{\otimes 3} form the line spanned by the q-antisymmetric vector \varepsilon_q, and each braid generator acts on \varepsilon_q as -q^{-1}.
  3. On the colour-singlet sector X = -q^{-1} b, and the rescaled generator satisfies -q X = b.
  4. For a braid word w with exponent sum e(w) and any linear trace \tau, the value of \tau on w evaluated in the generators X is (-q^{-1})^{e(w)} times its value in the generators b. Evaluated in the rescaled generators -qX, every value equals its flavour value.
prf:colour-singlet-flavour-generator: Proof Proof of the colour-singlet flavour generator. For item 1, direct matrix computation on (K^3)^{\otimes 3} verifies that Jimbo's \check R satisfies the quadratic Hecke relation, the braid relation \check R_{12}\check R_{23}\check R_{12} = \check R_{23}\check R_{12}\check R_{23}, and commutes with the three-fold coproducts of E_i, F_i, and L_j. For item 2, solving E_i v = F_i v = 0 and L_j v = v in (K^3)^{\otimes 3} under q \neq 0 and q^2 + 1 \neq 0 shows that the U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3)-invariant subspace is one-dimensional and spanned by the q-antisymmetric vector \varepsilon_q, on which \check R_{12} and \check R_{23} each act by the scalar -q^{-1}. Item 3 follows immediately on K\varepsilon_q \otimes W: since \check R_{\mathrm{colour}} acts as -q^{-1}, the tensor braiding X = \check R_{\mathrm{colour}} \cdot b restricts to -q^{-1} b, and multiplying by -q recovers b. For item 4, scaling every generator by a central scalar c multiplies the evaluation of a braid word w of exponent sum e(w) by c^{e(w)}, and linearity of \tau pulls c^{e(w)} out of \tau(w); setting c = -q^{-1} gives the raw-generator factor, and setting c = 1 for -qX gives exact agreement with the flavour trace.
rem:colour-singlet-rescaled-bond-law:
Remark Bond factors are stated in the rescaled generator. With Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the proton--proton bond factor in the flavour generator is z. In the raw generators it becomes -q^{-1} z = -q^2/(q^2+1), which is negative for real q > 0, so a bond law of the form \log(1/f) is stated in the rescaled generators b = -qX. With that choice every Markov trace value of a hadron word on the colour-singlet sector, and every per-bond factor, is the flavour value.

The \mathfrak{gl}_6 coideal route gives the singlet generator -b^{-1}, the image of b under the Hecke involution \sigma \mapsto -\sigma^{-1}; it satisfies (-b^{-1})(-q^{-1} b) = q^{-1}, so the two routes agree on the singlet sector up to that involution.
prop:colour-singlet-exterior-flavour-sym:
Proposition A colour-singlet state is q-exterior exactly when its flavour part is q-symmetric. Let K be a field, q \in K with q \neq 0, let M be a K-vector space with linear maps B_1, B_2 : M \to M, and on three strands let X_1 = \check R_{12} \otimes B_1 and X_2 = \check R_{23} \otimes B_2 act on (K^3)^{\otimes 3} \otimes M, where \check R is Jimbo's braiding of U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3). Call a state w q-exterior if X_1 w = -w and X_2 w = -w. For f \in M:

  1. \varepsilon_q \otimes f is q-exterior if and only if B_1 f = q f and B_2 f = q f.
  2. If B_1 f = -q^{-1} f, then X_1(\varepsilon_q \otimes f) = q^{-2}\, \varepsilon_q \otimes f, and q^{-2} \neq -1 whenever q^2 + 1 \neq 0.
prf:colour-singlet-exterior-flavour-symm: Proof Proof that colour-singlet q-exterior states are flavour q-symmetric. Each \check R_{i,i+1} acts on \varepsilon_q by -q^{-1}, so X_i(\varepsilon_q \otimes f) = \varepsilon_q \otimes (-q^{-1} B_i f). The (0,1,2) component of \varepsilon_q is 1, so \varepsilon_q \otimes g = \varepsilon_q \otimes h forces g = h. Hence X_i(\varepsilon_q \otimes f) = -\varepsilon_q \otimes f if and only if -q^{-1} B_i f = -f, that is B_i f = q f. For item 2, substitute B_1 f = -q^{-1} f: if q^{-2} = -1, then q^2 \cdot q^{-2} = 1 gives q^2 + 1 = 0, contradicting q^2 + 1 \neq 0.
rem:colour-flavour-mirror:
Remark The colour column pairs with the flavour row. The colour singlet \varepsilon_q spans the column (1^3) of (K^3)^{\otimes 3}. The proposition says that inside the q-exterior states its flavour partner lies in the row (3): colour and flavour carry transposed partitions. This is the colour-singlet slice of quantum skew Howe duality, in which the q-exterior algebra of colour \otimes flavour pairs each colour shape \lambda with the flavour shape \lambda'. The transposition \lambda \mapsto \lambda' is the Hecke involution \sigma \mapsto -\sigma^{-1} that the \mathfrak{gl}_6 coideal route applies to the flavour generator.

The tensor route and the coideal route therefore describe one structure. In the tensor route colour is a separate symmetry commuting with the braid; in the coideal route the antisymmetry of the colour singlet is carried into the flavour generator. At q = 1, item 1 is the familiar statement that a totally antisymmetric three-strand state whose colour part is the singlet has a totally symmetric flavour part.
prop:colour-relabel-singlet: Proposition Swapping two colours preserves the quantum singlet only at q squared equal to one. Let K be a field and q \in K^\times. Let \varepsilon_q \in (K^3)^{\otimes 3} be the quantum colour singlet of Jimbo's braiding on K^3, normalised by \varepsilon_q(0,1,2) = 1. Let s be the permutation of the colour labels exchanging 0 and 1, and let (s\cdot w)(a,b,c) = w(s(a), s(b), s(c)). Then s \cdot \varepsilon_q is a scalar multiple of \varepsilon_q if and only if q^2 = 1. When q^2 = 1 the scalar is -q^{-1}.
prf:colour-relabel-singlet:
Proof Proof that a colour swap fixes the singlet line only at q squared equal to one. The entries of \varepsilon_q on the six permutations (0,1,2), (0,2,1), (1,0,2), (1,2,0), (2,0,1), (2,1,0) are 1, -q^{-1}, -q^{-1}, q^{-2}, q^{-2}, -q^{-3}, and all other entries vanish.

Suppose s \cdot \varepsilon_q = c\,\varepsilon_q. At (0,1,2) this reads \varepsilon_q(1,0,2) = c, so c = -q^{-1}. At (1,0,2) it reads \varepsilon_q(0,1,2) = c\,\varepsilon_q(1,0,2), that is 1 = q^{-2}, so q^2 = 1.

Conversely, if q^2 = 1 then q^{-2} = 1 and q^{-3} = q^{-1}. Comparing s\cdot\varepsilon_q with -q^{-1}\varepsilon_q entry by entry on the six permutations gives -q^{-1} = -q^{-1}, q^{-2} = q^{-2}, 1 = q^{-2}, -q^{-1} = -q^{-3}, -q^{-3} = -q^{-3} and q^{-2} = q^{-4}, each of which holds. \blacksquare
rem:colour-relabel:
Remark Colour-tube sheets and the ordered colour basis. The three sheets r, g, b of the colour tube over Bring's surface represent the three colour states of a strand. Jimbo's braiding needs more than a set of three states: it needs them in an order, because its (q - q^{-1}) term sits only on ordered pairs. The proposition shows this order is real structure at generic q. Exchanging two colours does not send the singlet \varepsilon_q to a multiple of itself unless q^2 = 1.

Going around a branch point of the colour tube exchanges two sheets. So the identification of the sheets with an ordered basis of K^3 holds on a patch of the surface, not globally. Changing the order conjugates the braiding by the relabelling and carries \varepsilon_q to the singlet of the conjugated braiding, so every trace is unchanged. The two uses of the word colour therefore agree, and the ordering is a local choice that no observable sees.
prop:colour-braid-commuting-singlet: Proposition A linear map commuting with the colour braiding keeps the singlet line. Let K be a field and q \in K^\times with q^2 + 1 \neq 0. Let \check R_{12}, \check R_{23} be Jimbo's braidings on (K^3)^{\otimes 3}, and let \Phi be a K-linear map of (K^3)^{\otimes 3} with \Phi \check R_{12} = \check R_{12} \Phi and \Phi \check R_{23} = \check R_{23} \Phi. Then \Phi(\varepsilon_q) is a scalar multiple of \varepsilon_q. In particular, if the colour swap s of the colour-relabel proposition commuted with both braidings, then q^2 = 1.
prf:colour-braid-commuting-singlet:
Proof Proof that a braid-commuting map keeps the singlet line. Both braidings act on \varepsilon_q by -q^{-1}. By linearity and commutation, \check R_{12}\Phi(\varepsilon_q) = \Phi(\check R_{12}\varepsilon_q) = -q^{-1}\Phi(\varepsilon_q), and likewise for \check R_{23}. When q \neq 0 and q^2 + 1 \neq 0, the tensors on which both braidings act by -q^{-1} are exactly the multiples of \varepsilon_q. So \Phi(\varepsilon_q) = c\,\varepsilon_q with c its (0,1,2) entry.

For the last claim, the colour swap s is linear. If it commuted with both braidings, then s \cdot \varepsilon_q would be a multiple of \varepsilon_q, and by the colour-relabel proposition that forces q^2 = 1. \blacksquare
conj:colour-tube-monodromy-braided:
Conjecture Colour-tube monodromy commutes with the colour braiding. Going once around a branch point of the colour tube over Bring's surface acts on the three-strand colour space (K^3)^{\otimes 3} by a K-linear map that commutes with Jimbo's braidings \check R_{12} and \check R_{23}. That map is not the bare permutation of the two colliding sheets. It is that permutation corrected by the braiding, in the manner of the quantum Weyl group of U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) [lusztig1993].

If the conjecture holds, the commuting-singlet proposition shows that the monodromy keeps the colour singlet \varepsilon_q up to a scalar for every q with q^2 + 1 \neq 0. The identification of the tube's sheets with an ordered colour basis would then hold globally, up to that correction. The expectation comes from the Drinfeld–Kohno theorem: the monodromy of a flat connection on configuration space with values in a representation is computed by the braiding [kohno1987, drinfeld1990]. What is not shown is that the colour cubic on Bring's surface carries such a connection, and that its branch-point monodromy is the corrected swap.
rem:braid-base-field:
Remark Independence from the base field. The result braid action on tensor products uses only the braided monoidal structure of \mathbf{C}. In particular:

  1. For the archimedean realisation (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe), the braiding is computed by the R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)). The B_n-action recovers standard skein relations as traces on braid-group representations.
  2. For the \mathfrak{p}-adic realisation (p-adic realisation), the same braiding exists on \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_{q(p)}(2)) over \mathbb{Q}_\mathfrak{p}. The Yang--Baxter equation holds generically over any base ring.
  3. For the finite-field realisation (finite field realisation), the braiding persists on the fusion category \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)).

The skein relations, knot invariants, and hyperbolic volumes that appear in the archimedean setting are therefore consequences of the categorical braiding evaluated via a specific fibre functor. They are not the source of the braid-group structure.
rem:braid-lifting-compatibility:
Remark Compatibility with the lifting theorem. The jet prolongation is compatible with the braided monoidal structure. Suppose \mathbf{C} is braided with braiding c, and each level A_{n+1} = J^1(A_n) of the brane tower is an object of \mathbf{C}, with the section \ell_n\colon A_n \to A_{n+1} and left inverse r_n\colon A_{n+1} \to A_n morphisms of \mathbf{C}. Nothing has to be inherited: every pair of objects already carries the braiding c. What the tower needs is that the transition maps respect it, and this is naturality of c:

  (\ell_n \otimes \ell_n) \circ c_{A_n, A_n} = c_{A_{n+1}, A_{n+1}} \circ (\ell_n \otimes \ell_n),

and likewise for r_n. Applied factor by factor, \ell_n^{\otimes k} and r_n^{\otimes k} intertwine the braid-group representations \rho_k on A_n^{\otimes k} and A_{n+1}^{\otimes k}. The direct-limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim\Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) therefore carries a well-defined B_k-action for every k.
sec:categorical-braiding-hecke-eigenbasi: The group algebra of the braid group B_n has infinite rank and cannot support a finite-dimensional trace functional directly. Imposing the quadratic skein relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 projects the braid action onto the finite-dimensional Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) of rank n! over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. Within H_n(q), the Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution \overline{\sigma_i} = \sigma_i^{-1} separates self-dual and anti-self-dual classes, while the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M collapses closed braids to a single Laurent rational invariant. Diagonalizing the central Jucys–Murphy operators in H_n(q) produces the knot eigenbasis in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A), which serves as the algebraic basis for all subsequent mass and binding evaluations.
rem:eigenbasis-structural-lemmas:
Remark Content/twist eigenbasis: structural lemmas behind the Wedderburn characters (Lean). The categorical-confinement proposition expresses every physical observable as a sum of Wedderburn residues, \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi_\lambda, with one term per Wedderburn channel V_\lambda. The content/twist eigenbasis organises these characters \chi_\lambda by their ribbon-twist eigenvalue \theta_\lambda = q^{2c(\lambda)}, which is the scalar by which the full twist \varDelta^2 \in Z(H_n(q)) acts on V_\lambda. Three structural properties characterise each \chi_\lambda(\beta):

  1. Parity. For a braid word \beta of length L, every Laurent exponent of \chi_\lambda(\beta)(q) has the same parity as L. Equivalently, \chi_\lambda(\beta)(-q) = (-1)^L\,\chi_\lambda(\beta)(q). This parity dictates which crossing-counts contribute to a given channel.

  2. Conjugation duality. The sign-twisted map \sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1} — an algebra automorphism, leaving the coefficients alone — swaps the seminormal eigenvalues q \leftrightarrow -q^{-1} and so intertwines V_\lambda with the conjugate channel V_{\lambda'}. At the level of characters this reads

      \chi_\lambda(-q^{-1}) = \chi_{\lambda'}(q),

    and combining it with the parity of item 1 gives the signed form \chi_\lambda(q^{-1}) = (-1)^{L}\chi_{\lambda'}(q) for a braid word of length L. This conjugation duality represents the matter/antimatter symmetry of the channel weights.

    Two cautions. The intertwiner is not the bar involution Bar-involution and its P_{\mathrm{avg}} / P_{\mathrm{skew}} projections: that map sends \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1} together with q \mapsto q^{-1}, and the two halves cancel on the spectrum, so it fixes each eigenchannel rather than exchanging them. The missing ingredient is exactly the sign. And the sign in the displayed identity is (-1)^L, a function of the word, not a per-channel constant \varepsilon_\lambda: on every channel tested, including the self-conjugate (2,1) of H_3, it takes both values as L varies. Verified on H_2 and H_3 over all positive braid words with L \leq 6.

  3. Framing rational. Framing \beta by m full twists scales \chi_\lambda by \theta_\lambda^m. The framing tower is given by the single-pole rational function \chi_\lambda(\beta)/(1 - t\,\theta_\lambda), with its sole pole at t = q^{-2c(\lambda)}. This rational form determines how reframing redistributes weight across the tower.

These structural properties strictly derive from categorical inputs, namely the ribbon eigenvalue and the seminormal eigenvalue swap q \leftrightarrow -q^{-1}.
rem:markov-axioms-primitive:
Remark Primitive Markov-trace axioms (M1–M4 from Jones 1985 and Wenzl 1988). Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^{\times} an invertible element with a chosen square root q^{1/2}. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is the unique linear functional satisfying:

  1. Normalisation: \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.
  2. Cyclicity: \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx) for all x, y.
  3. Stabilisation by \sigma_n: \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_n(R, q), where z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the Markov-trace loop value (forced, see below).

Stabilisation by \sigma_n^{-1} — often listed as a fourth axiom — is not an independent condition. Substituting the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - (q - q^{-1}) into axiom 3 and using linearity of the trace (with x \cdot 1 = x) forces

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n^{-1}) \;=\; z_{-} \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x),
  \qquad
  z_{-} \;:=\; z - (q - q^{-1}),

so the negative-crossing loop value z_{-} differs from z whenever q \neq \pm 1. No choice of trace parameter makes the two stabilisations scale by mutually inverse factors either: z \cdot z_{-} = 1 has the sole solutions z = q and z = -q^{-1}, the one-dimensional characters of H_n(R, q), both of which are degenerate. Link invariance of the Jones polynomial is instead restored by the writhe prefactor outside the trace.

Axioms 1–2 with an unspecified stabilisation parameter admit a one-parameter family; axiom 3 selects one member of it, and which member is not free.

Given y_{(1^3)} = 0, the faithful normalised Markov trace is unique and has loop parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). The competing root z = q is real but degenerate (y_{(2,1)} = 0, not faithful on \mathrm{TL}_3), which is why the faithfulness hypothesis is load-bearing. Because y_{(1^3)} = 0, \mathrm{tr}_M factors through the Temperley–Lieb quotient and evaluates braid closures to the Jones polynomial.

Because \mathrm{tr}_M is compatible with the tower inclusions and evaluates disjoint generators by iterated application of axiom 3, the joint Markov trace of two braids acting on disjoint strand sets is strictly multiplicative:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(K_1 \sqcup K_2) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(K_1) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(K_2).

Appending k further strands, each stabilised by one positive crossing, multiplies this value by z^k (one factor of z per application of axiom 3). This derives the inter-knot decoupling theorem from primitive Markov axioms.
thm:jones-markov-trace:
Theorem Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987). Let q \in \mathbb{C}^{\times} not be a root of unity. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(\mathbb{C}, q) admits a unique \mathbb{C}-linear functional \mathrm{tr}_M satisfying:

  1. Normalisation: \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.
  2. Trace property: \mathrm{tr}_M(ab) = \mathrm{tr}_M(ba).
  3. Markov property, for x \in H_n(\mathbb{C}, q):
  \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x), \qquad
  z = \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} = \frac{q^2}{[2]_q} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i)

the Markov-trace loop value, with z(q_0) \approx 0.61268803714646525160. Under the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}, the Temperley–Lieb generator is e_i := q - \sigma_i, satisfying e_i^2 = [2]_q e_i with loop parameter \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. The value z = q^3/(q^2+1) reproduces the Jones–Temperley–Lieb normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(e_i) = q - z = q/(q^2+1) = 1/[2]_q = 1/\delta; this parameter is forced rather than stipulated: see Primitive Markov-trace axioms.

For each partition \lambda \vdash n, the restriction of \mathrm{tr}_M to the irreducible H_n(\mathbb{C}, q)-module S_\lambda is the scalar multiple y_\lambda \chi_\lambda, with explicit Young-diagram weights given by Vaughan F. R. Jones [jones1987], Hans Wenzl [wenzl1988], Rosa C. Orellana [orellana1998], and Meinolf Geck and Sofia Lambropoulou [geck-lambropoulou-2004]. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) that scalar vanishes precisely when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3: the fibre V is the two-dimensional fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) [jimbo1986], so no partition with three or more rows survives Schur–Weyl, and \mathrm{tr}_M is faithful on the two-row partitions and on nothing else. The vanishing blocks span the radical of the trace form; the quotient is the algebra of Harold Neville Vazeille Temperley and Elliott H. Lieb [temperley-lieb1971], H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n(q), and the surviving \sum \dim^2 is the Catalan number C_n — 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429 for n = 2, \ldots, 7. For any braid \beta, \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_n(\beta)) computes the Jones polynomial of the closure \hat{\beta} up to framing.
rem:jones-markov-trace-stabilisation: Remark Negative stabilisation and the Jones normalisation parameter. Stabilisation by \sigma_n^{-1} is forced by the Hecke quadratic relation: \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n^{-1}) = z_{-}\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) with z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}) (Markov axioms). The two loop values are distinct, and invariance of the resulting link polynomial under both Markov moves is achieved by a writhe-dependent prefactor outside the trace, not by symmetry of the trace itself.
rem:jones-markov-trace-formalization-not: Remark Formalization strategy for the Markov trace: axiomatic encoding of the three Jones properties. The existence proof of the Markov trace occupies §3–5 of Jones (1987). The result is taken as given rather than reproved, and only its core properties over the ground ring R_q = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] are used. Downstream results, such as completeness on irreducibles, are derived from these properties alone.
rem:markov-disambiguation:
Remark Three uses of Markov in this paper. Three constructs bear the name "Markov":

  1. Markov trace: The algebraic functional \mathrm{tr}_M on the Hecke algebra that feeds the mass formula.
  2. Markov chain: The stochastic random walk on braid words induced by Hecke transition probabilities, which provides error bounds.
  3. Markov moves: The topological operations of conjugation and stabilisation that generate link equivalence. Context clarifies usage, but when precision is needed, \mathrm{tr}_M denotes the algebraic functional, "Markov chain" the stochastic process, and "Markov move" the topological equivalence.

The trace does not require a closure; the topological reading does

A distinction the three senses above leave implicit, and which is load-bearing.

\mathrm{tr}_M is defined on all of H_n(q) by cyclicity together with the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x). It is a linear functional on an algebra, and it evaluates on any Hecke element — no braid, no closure, and no topology are needed for the number to exist.

What the closure supplies is the interpretation. By Markov's theorem two braids have the same closure exactly when they are related by conjugation and stabilisation; because \mathrm{tr}_M is invariant under both (modulo the writhe prefactor of the stabilisation remark), it descends to a link invariant on closures. That descent is what licenses reading \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) as a property of the link K_\beta.

Consequently, for W \in H_n(q) that is not in the image of \rho : B_n \to H_n(q), \mathrm{tr}_M(W) is a well-defined number with no link behind it. Such a W decomposes as a weighted sum of braid images, so \mathrm{tr}_M(W) is a weighted sum of link invariants — not the invariant of any one link. Any construction that reads a topological quantity off \mathrm{tr}_M(W) (a volume, a crossing number, a genus) must first establish that W is a braid image; linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M does not transport such quantities, because they are not linear.

The consequence matters in practice: an element whose letters are of the form c\,\sigma_g + d\,\mathbf{1} rather than braid generators has a well-defined Markov trace, but no hyperbolic volume can be read off it.
prop:trace-locality-meets-gs-non-localit:
Proposition Markov locality of single Hecke crossings. Markov locality. For every x \in H_n(q),

  \mathrm{tr}_{M, n+1}(x \sigma_n) = z\, \mathrm{tr}_{M, n}(x), \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_{M, n+1}(x \sigma_n^{-1}) = z_{-}\, \mathrm{tr}_{M, n}(x), \qquad
  z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}).

A single newly-added crossing contributes a scalar — depending only on the crossing sign — independent of the upstream history.
rem:trace-locality-product-factorisation:
Remark Product factorisation over the normal form: what has been checked. The proposition separates two facts: the Markov trace is local in a single newly added crossing, and the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form depends on the whole word. A third statement is often attached to them, that the Markov trace of the normal form factorises over its letters,

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_{\mathrm{NF}}(\beta)) = \prod_{i=1}^{M} \widehat{V}_i(q),

with each factor depending only on its own normal-form generator and the Bratteli path it traces through H_1 \subset H_2 \subset \cdots. This is not a theorem of the paper. The factors \widehat{V}_i have no definition yet, and the Markov trace is not multiplicative, so no argument from the trace alone gives a product.

What has been checked is the input such a factorisation would rest on. Over \mathbb{Q}(q) at generic q, the Wedderburn decomposition

  H_n(R, q) \otimes_R \mathbb{Q}(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} \mathrm{End}_{\mathbb{Q}(q)}(S^\lambda_q)

holds, and the Markov trace restricted to each block is a multiple w_\lambda(q) of the standard trace [wenzl1988]. The closed form

  w_\lambda(q) = \prod_{x \in \lambda} \frac{z\,q^{c(x)} - z_{-}\,q^{-c(x)}}{q^{h(x)} - q^{-h(x)}}, \qquad z_{-} = z - (q - q^{-1}),

where c(x) and h(x) are the content and hook length of the cell x, has been checked exactly for every \lambda \vdash n \le 5. Turning this into the product above needs a definition of \widehat{V}_i in terms of the Bratteli path and a proof that the block weights compose along it. Both remain to be done.
rem:trace-locality-gs-non-locality:
Remark Gröbner–Shirshov reduction is non-local. Let \beta = \sigma_{i_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_N} have Gröbner–Shirshov normal form \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\beta) = e_{j_1} \cdots e_{j_M}. Unlike the Markov locality of prop:trace-locality-meets-gs-non-locality, the reduction to normal form is non-local. This is an informal observation; no precise statement of it is proved here.

The Gröbner–Shirshov reduction algorithm on the Hecke algebra applies three rewriting rules:

  • Hecke quadratic relation: \sigma_i^2 \to (q - q^{-1}) \sigma_i + 1 (eliminates squared generators).
  • Braid relation: \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \to \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} (Yang–Baxter / commutation).
  • Far-commutativity: \sigma_i \sigma_j \to \sigma_j \sigma_i for \lvert i - j \rvert \geq 2.

The braid relation acts on a window of three consecutive generators, and successive applications can propagate changes across the entire braid word. Therefore the normal form depends non-locally on the input — flipping a single generator in \beta can require rewriting many generators in \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\beta).

Reconciliation. Markov locality and this non-locality concern different operations. The first is a property of the trace and the second a property of the reduction to normal form, so they do not conflict: the composite \beta \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) passes through the non-local map \beta \mapsto \mathrm{NF}_{\mathrm{GS}}(\beta), and the trace is then evaluated on the normal form.

Whether the trace of the normal form factorises over its letters is discussed in the product-factorisation check.
